title: What to Evaluate When Choosing a Property Management System
summary: See what to evaluate when choosing a property management system for short-stay rentals, from channel manager to finance.
body_markdown:
Choosing a **property management system** for short-stay rentals means evaluating two different layers: the channel manager, which syncs reservations across platforms like Airbnb and Booking (tools like Guesty or Stays cover this part), and the operational layer behind it, covering finance, approvals, and maintenance, where a system like **Jestor** comes in as a complement.


Many short-stay operators pick the right channel manager and only later realize that synced reservations don't cover finance, maintenance, or internal team communication.


These two layers rarely come from the same tool, and understanding that early avoids the search for one system that tries to do everything poorly.


## What's Often Missing After the Channel Manager


- Financial control by property, with organized payables and receivables
- An approval workflow for maintenance expenses above a set amount
- A standardized cleaning and check-in checklist, with an owner and deadline for each task
- Centralized communication with owners and field teams, without relying only on a WhatsApp group
- A consolidated view of how many properties have pending items in each area at once


## How to Evaluate Both Layers Together


1. Confirm the chosen channel manager syncs well with the platforms your operation uses
2. Map what falls outside that sync: finance, maintenance, approvals, internal communication
3. Check whether a system covers that operational side without needing a parallel spreadsheet
4. Assess whether that system integrates with the ERP used for the operation's finances
5. Test whether the field team can report issues and complete tasks from their phone


Layer What it covers


Channel manager Syncing reservations across platforms like Airbnb and Booking


Internal operations system Finance, approvals, maintenance, and team communication


## Why **Jestor** Complements This Operation


- Approval workflows with **spending limits** for maintenance expenses, without relying on spreadsheets or email
- Native integration with **Omie** and **Conta Azul** for property-level finance
- **Tasks** with subtasks for cleaning and check-in checklists, with deadlines and owners
- Integrated **WhatsApp Business** , centralizing communication with owners and field teams


## Frequently asked questions


**Does Jestor replace the operation's channel manager?** No, **Jestor** complements the operational side (finance, approvals, maintenance) that the channel manager doesn't cover.


**Can multiple properties be tracked from a single dashboard?** Yes, a dashboard consolidates finance, tasks, and approvals by property; see more at[jestor.com](https://www.jestor.com/?ref=blog.jestor.com) .


**Do you need to switch channel managers to use this operational system?** No, it works as a complementary layer, independent of whatever channel manager the operation already uses.


**Can the field team use this from their phone?** Yes, tasks and checklists are also accessible through the mobile version.


Accounting for both layers of a **property management system** , reservations and internal operations, avoids the search for one single tool that tries to cover everything poorly.
